title: When the position makes a quiet move right
outcomes: Predicts that a pinned knight or a settled centre can make a quiet pawn move the right move
Names the default the move overrides: develop a piece first, or do not waste time on a rook pawn
Sees when the same quiet move costs time because development is unfinished

steps.text: **Develop, wait or answer: choosing without a label** gave rook-pawn moves a concrete job. Here the *character* of the position decides. A pinned knight lets a pawn ask the pinning bishop a question. A settled centre, where neither side has a profitable break, takes the rush out of the game. Each such move overrides a default; name it.

The default to name is the one the move overrides. Against a pin, the default is *develop a piece first*. In a settled centre it is *do not waste time on a rook pawn*. *Rule of thumb:* a pin or a settled centre can make a quiet pawn move right. With no pin and the pieces still at home, the same move costs a tempo.

steps.title: The same pawn move at two moments
steps.prompt: White plays a3 at move 14 in a settled Spanish and at move 6 in the same opening with most pieces at home. Predict whether it does a job in each, then check.
For each of the two quiet moves in this lesson, write the default it overrode and the feature of the position that allowed it. Which of those features can you spot in your own games?
